title: Your First Job in Canada
intro_es: Los primeros días en un trabajo nuevo marcan mucho: llega preparado y con confianza.
paragraphs: Your first job in Canada is an exciting step. It may not be the job you had in Mexico, and that is normal. Many newcomers start in a position below their experience while they build Canadian contacts and confidence. Every job is a chance to practise English, understand workplace culture and add a Canadian reference to your résumé.

The first days are usually called onboarding. You will probably fill out forms, give your Social Insurance Number for payroll, set up direct deposit and complete safety training. Some workplaces give you a buddy, a coworker who helps you learn the routines. Many jobs also have a probation period, often the first few months, when your employer checks if the job is a good fit.

Small talk is an important part of work life in Canada. In the kitchen or before a meeting, people often chat about the weather, sports, food or their plans. These short conversations build trust. You don't need perfect English. A simple question like “Did you do anything fun this weekend?” is enough to start. Listen, smile and share a little about yourself too.

Many newcomers are afraid to ask questions because they don't want to look incompetent. In Canada, asking questions is usually seen as a good thing. It shows that you care about doing the job right. Try phrases like “Could you walk me through this?” or “Just to make sure I understand, you want me to...?” If you didn't hear something, it is fine to say, “Sorry, could you repeat that?”

Pay attention to workplace expectations. Arrive on time, tell your manager early if you are sick and follow the rules for breaks. When you get paid, read your pay stub to check your hours and deductions, such as income tax and pension contributions.

Finally, be patient with yourself. The first months can be tiring, especially when you work in a second language. Celebrate small wins, ask for feedback and keep learning. Step by step, you will feel more confident.
